summary: The joke that lands wrong: Asked about {the matter} at {the event}, you make a joke, and it lands on the wrong people.
realLife: One life: In 2004 his line explaining that he voted for war funding before voting against it became his opponents' theme. In 2006 a joke about students getting stuck in Iraq drew attacks; he apologized after two days and dropped plans to run again. Another: Asked about the bridge lane closures in December 2013, he joked that he worked the cones himself.
gates: You hold an office or are campaigning.
Your remark is on record from a public event or a reporter.
weights: How hurt the people it hit are.
choices: call it a botched joke and refuse to apologize
apologize after a day or two

branches.when: you wait two days to apologize
branches.then: Your own party's candidates ask you to stay away, and you give up a run you had planned.

branches.when: the joke was about a scandal that grows
branches.then: The line is replayed every time a new email comes out (C21).
